title: Morning calibration failure report
summary: ReMotion received a profile assigned to Trainer-2.
content:
Automated calibration test log:
Robot: REMOTION-01
Requested profile: REMOTION-01-DEFAULT
Received profile: TRAINER-2
Exercise mode: upper-limb-assisted
Result: PROFILE_HARDWARE_MISMATCH
Action taken: pre-movement lockout, emergency stop armed.
The test harness confirms the mismatch was detected before any actuator command was issued.

title: Robot diagnostic log
summary: Sequence of profile request, rejection, and emergency stop.
content:
06:47:58 - Startup sequence initiated by REMOTION-01
06:48:01 - Calibration profile requested from calibration-service
06:48:03 - Profile TRAINER-2 returned by calibration-service
06:48:04 - Local safety check: shoulder rotation limit mismatch (expected <=72deg, profile specifies <=58deg)
06:48:04 - Profile rejected by onboard safety controller
06:49:00 - Emergency stop activated, actuators locked
The robot's local safety system behaved correctly throughout this sequence.

title: Calibration profile comparison
summary: Side-by-side comparison of the ReMotion and Trainer-2 calibration profiles.
content:
Property | ReMotion | Trainer-2
Maximum shoulder rotation | 72deg | 58deg
Resistance limit | 18 Nm | 12 Nm
Sensor-array version | S4 | S2
Exercise mode | upper-limb-assisted | upper-limb-assisted
The two profiles are for physically different hardware configurations. Loading Trainer-2's profile onto ReMotion would allow movement commands that exceed Trainer-2's safe limits, which is why the onboard safety controller intervened.

title: Patch Vector's safety report
summary: Patch warned that calibration profiles might remain cached too long and recommended delaying the demonstration.
content:
Internal safety memo, Patch Vector:
'During review of the calibration-service cache layer, I found that profile cache keys are not strictly scoped per-robot under certain restart conditions. In the worst case a robot could receive a cached profile belonging to a different unit. I recommend we delay the public demonstration until the cache-key scoping is fixed and re-tested.'

title: Demonstration decision
summary: Signal approved the demonstration despite Patch's unresolved technical concerns.
content:
Email thread, subject 'Re: Demo go/no-go':
Signal Scholar: 'Understood, but we cannot slip the date again. Unless someone can show me a concrete failure, we proceed as planned. Log it as a known risk and move on.'
Patch Vector: 'Noted. For the record, I don't think this is purely theoretical.'
